questions.title: Chronic inflammation identified from a gastric-ulcer biopsy
questions.question: A 60 year old female with gastric ulcer. The biopsy revealed infiltration by lymphocytes and plasma cells with evidence of tissue destruction. This indicates:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Acute inflammation is dominated by neutrophils and abundant edema fluid, not by lymphocytes and plasma cells, and it is a short-lived response rather than the prolonged, destruction-with-healing picture described.
explanations.B: Correct. Infiltration by mononuclear cells -- lymphocytes, plasma cells and macrophages -- is the pathologic hallmark of chronic inflammation, distinct from the neutrophil-dominated picture of acute inflammation. A chronic gastric ulcer is a classic example in which continuing tissue injury and attempted healing by fibrosis proceed together, so the coexistence of a mononuclear infiltrate with evidence of tissue destruction points specifically to chronicity. Plasma cells are B lymphocytes that have transformed into antibody-secreting cells, and their presence alongside lymphocytes is the expected chronic-inflammatory response at a persistent ulcer.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Hyperplastic change is an increase in the number of cells of a tissue, not an inflammatory infiltrate; the biopsy describes an infiltrate of inflammatory cells with tissue destruction, which is not what hyperplasia means.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Malignant transformation would be recognised by cellular and nuclear pleomorphism, atypical mitoses and invasion, none of which are described here -- a lymphocyte-and-plasma-cell infiltrate is a reactive inflammatory finding, not evidence of malignancy.

questions.learning_objective: Identify a mononuclear (lymphocyte and plasma cell) infiltrate with ongoing tissue destruction as the hallmark of chronic inflammation.

questions.title: Healing by second intention
questions.question: Which of the following best describes healing by second intention:

options.A: Healing of large infected wound with extensive tissue loss
options.B: Restoration of tissue to normal without scar formation
options.C: The direct conversion of fibrin to collagen without inflammation
options.D: Healing of clean, uninfected surgical wound with sutured edges

explanations.A: Correct. Second intention healing is the mode used for open, gaping, infected or tissue-loss wounds, where the edges cannot simply be apposed. It closes through abundant granulation tissue growing from the base of the wound, takes longer than first intention, and is completed partly by myofibroblast-driven wound contraction. The large amount of granulation tissue and contraction leave a larger, less regular scar than the fine linear scar of first intention.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Restoration of tissue to normal without a scar is regeneration by labile or stable cells, not healing by second intention, which necessarily ends in a scar because it repairs by fibrosis.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Collagen is laid down by fibroblasts within granulation tissue during an inflammatory repair response; there is no direct fibrin-to-collagen conversion and healing is not an inflammation-free process.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Healing of a clean, uninfected, sutured surgical wound with apposed edges is first intention healing, which forms only a small amount of granulation tissue and a fine pale linear scar -- the opposite of the tissue-loss situation of second intention.

questions.learning_objective: Distinguish healing by second intention (open/infected/tissue-loss wounds, abundant granulation tissue, wound contraction) from first intention.
questions.module_subject: 208 INT > Healing and Repair > Wound Healing

questions.title: Histologic hallmark of an abscess
questions.question: Histologically, an abscess is characterized by which feature:

options.A: Diffuse involvement of tissue without a local collection
options.B: A thick capsule of mature scar tissue
options.C: A central zone of caseation necrosis
options.D: A localized collection of suppuration inflammatory tissue

explanations.A: Incorrect. Diffuse involvement of tissue without a walled-off local collection describes cellulitis (diffuse suppurative inflammation), which spreads because streptococcal fibrinolysin and hyaluronidase break down fibrin -- the opposite of an abscess.
explanations.B: Incorrect. An abscess is walled off by an acute pyogenic membrane and, only later, granulation tissue; a thick capsule of mature scar tissue is a feature of chronic walled-off lesions, not the defining histology of a suppurative abscess.
explanations.C: Incorrect. A central zone of caseation necrosis is the hallmark of a tuberculous (caseating granulomatous) lesion, not a pyogenic abscess, whose centre is liquefied pus rather than cheesy caseous material.
explanations.D: Correct. An abscess is a form of localized suppurative inflammation: a discrete, walled-off cavity containing pus -- neutrophils, pus cells, necrotic tissue and edema fluid. It is commonly caused by Staphylococcus aureus, whose coagulase converts fibrinogen to fibrin and walls the pus off into a local collection. This walling-off into a localized collection of suppuration is exactly what distinguishes an abscess from diffuse cellulitis.

questions.learning_objective: Define an abscess as a localized, walled-off collection of pus, contrasting it with diffuse cellulitis and caseating granulomas.

questions.title: Feature marking an inflammation as chronic
questions.question: The most characteristic feature that an inflammatory process has become chronic rather than acute is:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Dilatation of local capillaries (vascular congestion producing the redness and heat of inflammation) is a feature of the early acute vascular response, not a marker of chronicity.
explanations.B: Incorrect. A predominance of neutrophils is the hallmark of acute inflammation; chronic inflammation is defined instead by a mononuclear (lymphocyte, plasma cell, macrophage) infiltrate.
explanations.C: Correct. In chronic inflammation, continuing tissue injury and attempted healing proceed together, so the tissue simultaneously shows new blood vessel formation (angiogenesis) and fibrosis alongside the mononuclear infiltrate. This coexistence of ongoing repair -- angiogenesis and fibrosis -- with persisting inflammation is what most characteristically distinguishes a chronic process from an acute one. Acute inflammation, by contrast, shows vascular dilatation, edema and neutrophils without this concurrent fibrotic healing.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Predominant edema (protein-rich exudate) reflects the increased vascular permeability of acute inflammation; chronic inflammation shows relatively little edema fluid compared with the acute phase.

questions.learning_objective: Recognise concurrent angiogenesis and fibrosis (healing proceeding alongside injury) as the characteristic marker that inflammation has become chronic.

questions.title: Definition of margination
questions.question: During the process of acute inflammation, “margination” refers to which cellular behavior:

options.B: Leukocytes move from the central blood flow to the vessel wall
options.D: The clustering of RBCs in the center of blood vessel

explanations.A: Incorrect. Rapid proliferation of endothelial cells is a feature of angiogenesis during repair, not the definition of margination, which is a movement of leukocytes rather than a proliferative event.
explanations.B: Correct. Margination is the first step of leukocyte recruitment: as blood flow slows (stasis) at the inflamed site, neutrophils move out of the normal central (axial) stream into the peripheral plasmatic zone next to the endothelium. Positioned at the vessel wall, they can then roll (selectin-mediated), adhere firmly (integrin-mediated pavementing) and finally emigrate. So margination specifically names the redistribution of leukocytes from the centre of the flow to the vessel wall.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Leukocytes squeezing between endothelial cells through the vessel wall is emigration (transmigration/diapedesis), a later step that follows margination, rolling and firm adhesion.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Clustering of red cells in the centre of the vessel (rouleaux/axial packing from stasis) is a rheologic change that helps push leukocytes peripherally, but margination refers to the leukocytes moving to the wall, not to the red cells clustering centrally.

questions.learning_objective: Define margination as the movement of leukocytes from the central axial blood stream to the vessel wall, the first step of leukocyte recruitment.

questions.title: Malignancy complicating Schistosoma haematobium infection
questions.question: Chronic inflammation with Schistosoma haematobium may be complicated by the following type of malignancy:

options.D: Squamous cell carcinoma of the urinary bladder

explanations.A: Incorrect. Adenocarcinoma of the colon is associated with Schistosoma mansoni colonic disease and adenomatous change, not with Schistosoma haematobium, which is the urinary (vesical) species.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Renal cell carcinoma arises from renal tubular epithelium and has no established causal link to bilharzial infection; haematobium disease targets the bladder wall, not the renal parenchyma.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Gastric carcinoma is linked to Helicobacter pylori, chronic atrophic gastritis and intestinal metaplasia of the stomach, not to Schistosoma haematobium.
explanations.D: Correct. Schistosoma haematobium lodges in the vesical (bladder) plexus, and its chronic inflammation drives squamous metaplasia of the transitional (urothelial) lining. Squamous cell carcinoma of the urinary bladder is stated directly among the predisposing factors for squamous cell carcinoma as arising on top of this bilharzial squamous metaplasia. This is why bilharzial (schistosomal) cystitis is the classic cause of squamous -- rather than transitional-cell -- carcinoma of the bladder.

questions.subtopic: Metaplasia and predisposing factors for malignancy
questions.learning_objective: Link Schistosoma haematobium chronic cystitis, through squamous metaplasia, to squamous cell carcinoma of the urinary bladder.

questions.title: Most common bilharzial lesion of the colon
questions.question: The most common bilharzial lesion in the colon is:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Sandy patches (mucosal deposits of calcified dead ova) do occur in colonic bilharziasis, but they are not the most common lesion of the colon and are more characteristic of the urinary bladder.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Bilharzial ulcers are part of the colonic lesion spectrum but are less common than polyps at this site; the colon is wide and lesions are usually superficial.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Leukoplakia is a keratinizing white plaque of squamous or metaplastic squamous epithelium (mouth, bladder), not a lesion of the columnar-lined colon in bilharziasis.
explanations.D: Correct. Bilharziasis of the large intestine affects mainly the rectosigmoid segment, and bilharzial polyps are much more common in the colon than at any other site. They form as inflammatory/granulomatous outgrowths around deposited ova and typically present with bleeding. Their frequency at the rectosigmoid is why polyps are the most common colonic bilharzial lesion.

questions.learning_objective: Identify bilharzial polyps as the most common colonic (rectosigmoid) lesion of intestinal schistosomiasis.

questions.title: Opportunistic infections in AIDS (EXCEPT)
questions.question: Opportunistic infections in AIDS include all of the following EXCEPT:

explanations.A: Incorrect (it IS an opportunistic infection). Candidiasis is a fungal opportunistic infection of the AIDS crisis phase, and oral/oesophageal candidiasis is one of the common defining infections.
explanations.B: Correct (this is the EXCEPTION). Bilharziasis (schistosomiasis) is a primary parasitic infection acquired from contaminated fresh water, not an opportunistic infection that exploits the CD4 depletion of AIDS. The opportunistic infections that define the AIDS crisis phase are protozoal/helminthic (strongyloidiasis, pneumocystis), fungal (candidiasis, histoplasmosis, cryptococcosis), bacterial (tuberculosis, atypical mycobacteria, salmonella) and viral (CMV, HSV, EBV) -- bilharziasis is not on that list.
explanations.C: Incorrect (it IS an opportunistic infection). Pneumocystis (carinii/jirovecii) pneumonia is one of the classic AIDS-defining opportunistic infections.
explanations.D: Incorrect (it IS an opportunistic infection). Atypical (non-tuberculous) mycobacteria, such as Mycobacterium avium complex, are named bacterial opportunistic infections of advanced AIDS.

questions.learning_objective: Distinguish the opportunistic infections of the AIDS crisis phase from primary infections such as bilharziasis.

questions.title: False statement about AIDS
questions.question: Which of the following is FALSE about AIDS:

options.A: Homosexuals, Intravenous drug abusers and blood recipients are at high risk for developing AIDS
options.B: The causative virus is a retrovirus (RNA virus containing the enzyme reverse transcriptase)
options.C: Two types of the virus are known: 1 and 2
options.D: It is caused by Human Papilloma virus

explanations.A: Incorrect statement to pick (it is TRUE). Men who have sex with men, intravenous drug abusers and recipients of infected blood/blood products are recognised high-risk groups for HIV transmission.
explanations.B: Incorrect statement to pick (it is TRUE). HIV is a retrovirus -- an RNA virus that carries reverse transcriptase, which transcribes its RNA genome into DNA that integrates into the host cell.
explanations.C: Incorrect statement to pick (it is TRUE). Two types of the virus are recognised, HIV-1 and HIV-2.
explanations.D: Correct (this is the FALSE statement). AIDS is caused by the Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV), a retrovirus that selectively depletes CD4+ helper T cells -- not by the Human Papilloma virus. Human Papilloma virus causes genital warts and cervical carcinoma, an entirely different agent and disease. Naming HPV as the cause of AIDS is therefore the false statement.

questions.learning_objective: Identify HIV (a retrovirus) as the cause of AIDS and reject Human Papilloma virus as the causative agent.
